title: Bajío Corridor — $200M Industrial Real Estate Assessment
bluf: The Bajío corridor remains the premier nearshoring destination for mid-to-high-value manufacturing, but faces acute energy-infrastructure constraints that will define tenant viability over your 36-month horizon.

headline_judgments.claim: At least one sub-corridor will experience a material power disruption event (>4 hours unplanned CFE outage) within 12 months
headline_judgments.subscriber_action: Commission CFE substation reliability report before committing capital

headline_judgments.claim: Aguascalientes has the lowest per-capita water availability in the Bajío (1,200 m³/year vs 3,500 national average)
Guanajuato is too risky for new industrial capital until Q4 2026 at earliest
headline_judgments.subscriber_action: Do not commit new capital to Guanajuato industrial assets until Q4 2026

headline_judgments.claim: USMCA review (July 1, 2026) is the single largest macro risk to the Bajío thesis

subsections.title: Guanajuato (León–Silao–Irapuato–Celaya)
subsections.narrative: CJNG dominant after El Mencho's death. February 2026 operation aftermath: 70+ attacks across 23 municipalities, 60 arson incidents, 200+ Oxxo stores damaged. CJNG succession battle being fought on industrial corridors.

judgments.claim: One major industrial park will experience temporary shutdown due to cartel violence within 12 months
judgments.subscriber_action: Do not commit new capital to Guanajuato until Q4 2026

subsections.subscriber_action: Do not commit new capital to Guanajuato until Q4 2026. If existing exposure, secure 24/7 private security.

subsections.title: Querétaro (Querétaro City–San Juan del Río–El Marqués)
subsections.narrative: Lowest risk in the Bajío. Active security cordon at Guanajuato-Michoacán borders. However, post-Mencho violence pushes CJNG northward. Water scarcity is the primary risk — 15-20% water deficit by 2027 per CONAGUA.

judgments.claim: CJNG displaced elements will seek new extortion territories in Querétaro
judgments.subscriber_action: Prefer El Marqués parks with private water treatment plants

subsections.subscriber_action: Best entry point for first $50-75M. Require water-rights guarantees in lease agreements.

subsections.title: Aguascalientes (Aguascalientes City–Calvillo–Rincón de Romos)
subsections.narrative: Historical security outlier, but February 2026 road burnings signal material downgrade. Most acute water stress in the Bajío (1,200 m³/year per capita vs 3,500 national average).

judgments.claim: Material security event likely within 12 months
judgments.subscriber_action: Proceed with caution. Favor urban perimeter assets.

subsections.subscriber_action: Require water-rights audit and CFE substation reliability report before any acquisition.

subsections.title: CFE Grid Reliability
subsections.narrative: CFE 2026-2027 transmission expansion plan: new 400kV line Querétaro→Aguascalientes. Target Q4 2027. GAP: No verified construction progress data.

subsections.title: USMCA Review & Tariff Risk
subsections.narrative: July 1, 2026 deadline. Kalshi KXTARIFFRATEPRC markets imply ~13% probability of >9% tariff rate.

subsections.title: Water Security
subsections.narrative: CONAGUA 2026-2030 water availability update expected Q3 2026. El Zapotillo dam expansion is key upgrade signal.
subsections.subscriber_action: Monitor CONAGUA update — do not commit without water-rights guarantees

subsections.title: Natural Gas Access
subsections.narrative: Cenagas pipeline capacity auction June 2026. GAP: No current utilization data for Querétaro.
subsections.subscriber_action: Request Cenagas auction results when released
